notes: topics, sources and ruleVersions are imported into Sanity by studio/scripts/import-seed.ts.
sources[].role and sources[].curationNote are INTERNAL (evaluation answer key). Never write them into Knowledge Base files.
ruleVersions are imported as DRAFTS. A human checks each one against the official source (see checkFirst) and publishes it. Knowledge Base dataset sources read published documents only.
ids contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (no dots), so documents stay readable on a public dataset.

The seed owns only the fields it sets. A null field clears that field in the dataset; a field that is missing is left alone. Tool and reviewer fields (capturedAt, snapshotSha256, verification) are never written by the seed.

topics.title: NISA
topics.summary: Japan's tax-exempt individual investment account system (Nippon Individual Savings Account).

topics.title: Furusato nozei
topics.summary: Hometown tax donation system: donations to municipalities reduce income tax and residence tax.

sources.title: NISAを知る（NISA特設ウェブサイト）
sources.curationNote: Official overview of the 2024 NISA: tsumitate quota 3x old tsumitate NISA (¥1.2M/yr), growth quota 2x old general NISA (¥2.4M/yr), combined use up to ¥3.6M/yr, ¥18M lifetime limit with growth capped at ¥12M. Also gives the system's history (2014, 2016, 2018, 2024).

sources.title: 2023年までのNISA（NISA特設ウェブサイト）
sources.curationNote: Pre-2024 holdings keep their 5/20-year periods, no new purchases from 2024, cannot be moved into the new NISA, managed outside the ¥18M limit. Junior NISA balances withdrawable tax-free from 2024.

sources.title: NISAを利用する皆さまへ（令和6年6月・令和7年9月改訂）
sources.curationNote: Slide deck summarizing the current system: indefinite holding period, quotas, ¥18M lifetime limit (growth ¥12M).

sources.title: 令和8（2026）年度税制改正について－税制改正大綱における金融庁関係の主要項目－
sources.curationNote: Dec 2025 tax reform outline: tsumitate quota opened to ages 0-17 (¥600k/yr, ¥6M limit), guardian withdrawals from age 12 only with the child's consent; product scope changes.

sources.title: アクセスFSA 2026年2月号：令和8年度税制改正大綱における金融庁関係の主要項目について
sources.curationNote: Explains the reform: currently tsumitate requires age 18+; from January 2027 ages 0-17 get ¥600k/yr and ¥6M limit.

sources.title: NISAに関する情報
sources.curationNote: Procedures and NTA materials on NISA and Junior NISA; links to the FSA site.

sources.title: 賢く使おう「NISA」制度
sources.publisher: 財務省中国財務局 Chugoku Local Finance Bureau (Ministry of Finance)
sources.curationNote: One NISA account per person, institution changeable yearly; limits managed at book value; sold amounts reusable from the following year.

sources.title: Access FSA (2023, provisional translation): major expansion and perpetuation of NISA
sources.curationNote: Official English explanation of the planned new NISA, written before the January 2024 launch.

sources.title: FSA presentation (May 2025): complete revamp of NISA
sources.curationNote: English slides summarizing the January 2024 revamp and adoption figures. Carries a disclaimer that it may not reflect the official FSA view.

sources.title: 海外へ転居します。NISAの取引はどうなりますか。
sources.curationNote: Leaving Japan: departure notice closes the account; continuation notice (employer transfer or similar, incl. accompanying spouse) keeps holdings until Dec 31 of the year 5 years after the notice; no trading abroad; return notice needed.

sources.title: 海外赴任（非居住者）となった場合も、NISAの利用を継続したい。
sources.curationNote: Same continuation rule; Junior NISA excluded; account closed if no return notice within the period.

sources.title: 2027年開始！こども支援NISAとは？
sources.curationNote: Children's NISA from 2027-01-01 (0-17, ¥600k/yr, ¥6M, tsumitate products only, moves to adult NISA at 18); compares with Junior NISA (¥800k/yr, ended 2023).

sources.title: 18歳未満向け「こどもNISA」が税制大綱入り！
sources.curationNote: Written at the tax-reform-outline stage (Dec 2025); describes the minors' quota as a plan, not law. Tests outline-vs-enacted status.

sources.title: 海外赴任とNISA・iDeCo【2026年版】
sources.curationNote: Dates the continuation framework to the FY2019 tax reform; only employer-ordered moves qualify; documents broker differences (some brokers do not support continuation).

sources.title: NISAは駐在中どうなる？海外赴任前に必ず知っておくべき「5年間継続特例」の完全解説
sources.curationNote: Frames the 5-year continuation rule as part of the 2024 new NISA (rangsit dates it to 2019). Tests origin-date conflicts.

sources.title: 2027年NISA改正をわかりやすく解説
sources.curationNote: States the minors' change is in a law promulgated 2026-03-31, effective 2027-01-01. Verify enactment officially.

sources.title: よくわかる！ふるさと納税
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications

sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
sources.curationNote: One-stop only if donating to 5 or fewer municipalities; the ¥2,000 applies to the yearly total, not each donation.

sources.title: ふるさと納税について（指定基準に係る告示改正）令和8年3月24日
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
sources.curationNote: March 2026 revision of designation criteria: usable share moving toward 60%, designation revocation up to 3 years, look-back up to 5 years; portal fees ~13% of donations.

sources.title: ふるさと納税ポータルサイト（総務省）
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
sources.curationNote: Designation system in force since 2019-06-01: donations to non-designated municipalities do not qualify. Topic list includes 2026 designation notices.

sources.title: ふるさと納税の指定基準の見直し等（報道資料）
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications

sources.title: ふるさと納税、2025年10月からポイント付与伴う寄付禁止
sources.publisher: ネットショップ担当者フォーラム (Impress)
sources.curationNote: Reports the June 2024 notice: from October 2025, donations via portals granting points are banned, point sites included; card-payment points treated as ordinary.

sources.title: 楽天ふるさと納税におけるポイント付与ルール変更のおしらせ
sources.curationNote: Rakuten confirms portal points ended from 2025-10-01 following the June 2024 MIC notice.

sources.title: ふるさと納税 2026年10月改正｜何が変わり、何が変わらないか
sources.curationNote: Oct 2026 changes affect municipalities only; deduction mechanics and one-stop conditions (5 municipalities, Jan 10 arrival) unchanged.

sources.title: ふるさと納税、2026年10月から何が変わる？自治体側の規制強化と2027年寄付分の「193万円上限」
sources.curationNote: Frames the ¥1.93M special deduction cap as applying to donations from 2027. Pair with geisei (FY2028 residence tax framing): same rule, apparent conflict.

sources.title: 「ふるさと納税」2026年度改正で激変へ
sources.curationNote: Frames the ¥1.93M cap as applying from FY2028 residence tax; usable share 52.5% from Oct 2026, 55% from Oct 2027.

sources.title: ふるさと納税、2026年10月からルールが変わります
sources.publisher: クレド税理士事務所 Credo Tax Office
sources.curationNote: Frames the change as a cost cap shrinking from 50% to 47.5% (complement of the 52.5% usable share): same rule, apparent conflict.

sources.title: NISA and Retirement Saving For Foreign People in Japan

sources.curationNote: Says NISA is for residents over 20; gives pre-2024 limits. Accurate for its time, outdated now.

sources.title: Nippon individual savings account

sources.title: Regular NISA and Tsumitate NISA (forum thread)
sources.curationNote: Old thread: ¥400k/yr tsumitate for 20 years, age 20+.

sources.title: Unlocking NISA: The Essential Guide for Expats in Japan

sources.title: The New NISA Program: An Easy Walkthrough
sources.curationNote: Written before the 2024 launch (future tense); new limits correct.

sources.title: New NISA Complete Guide
sources.curationNote: Current limits; age 18+ as of January 1; one account per person; quota reuse.

sources.title: New NISA Glossary
sources.curationNote: English glossary of 2024 NISA terms: growth ¥2.4M/yr and ¥12M, tsumitate ¥1.2M/yr, ¥18M lifetime, indefinite period.

sources.title: What Is Furusato Nozei? The Japanese Tax Benefit That Gets You Free Stuff
sources.curationNote: Published before the October 2025 portal-point ban and the October 2026 changes. Check what it says about points at capture.

sources.title: Furusato Nozei Guide for Company Employees in Japan
sources.curationNote: Describes the one-stop limit as more than five donations; MIC sets it at five municipalities. Portal-point ban described correctly.

sources.title: 【2026】Furusato Nozei Guide for Foreigners: Lower Residence Tax & Get Rakuten Points
sources.curationNote: Labeled 2026 but recommends timing donations for Rakuten bonus-point campaigns, which the October 2025 ban ended.

sources.title: Furusato Nozei for Foreigners: Cut Your Japan Resident Tax
sources.curationNote: One-stop applications are voided if you file a tax return; repeat donations to one municipality count once toward the five.

sources.title: Furusato Nozei in Japan: A Foreign Resident's Complete Guide (2026)
sources.curationNote: Five municipalities, January 10 deadline, portal points ended October 2025, name must match residence record.

sources.title: Furusato Nozei for Foreigners in Japan: The Complete Guide (2026)
sources.curationNote: Notes the October 2025 ban on portal bonus points; ordinary card points unaffected.

sources.title: Japan Furusato Nozei Complete Guide
sources.curationNote: Point rewards ended October 2025; written early 2026, so no October 2026 changes.

sources.title: 平成26年度税制改正について－税制改正大綱における金融庁関係の主要項目－
sources.curationNote: Dec 2013 FY2014 tax reform summary. Until 2014: one NISA account per person, institution cannot be changed within the account period (up to 4 years), a closed account cannot be reopened in that period. From 2015: institution changeable once per year; reopening allowed.

sources.title: 平成27年度税制改正について－税制改正大綱における金融庁関係の主要項目－
sources.curationNote: Jan 2015 FY2015 tax reform summary: NISA annual limit raised from ¥1,000,000 to ¥1,200,000 (from 2016); Junior NISA created (investment from April 2016).

sources.title: 「金融商品取引業者等向けの総合的な監督指針」の一部改正（案）の公表について
sources.curationNote: Oct 2015 supervisory guideline amendment. States the NISA annual limit rises from ¥1,000,000 to ¥1,200,000 from January 2016 and Junior NISA starts April 2016.

sources.title: 個人の方が株式等や土地・建物等を譲渡した場合の令和8年度税制改正のあらまし
sources.curationNote: NTA outline (May 2026) of 所得税法等の一部を改正する法律 (令和8年法律第12号, promulgated 2026-03-31): from 2027-01-01, tsumitate quota for ages 0-17, ¥600,000/yr, ¥6,000,000 holding limit, automatic move at 18; from age 12, withdrawals only for the child's education or living costs.

sources.title: ふるさと納税の概要について
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
sources.curationNote: MIC overview with reform history (p.3): FY2008 reform introduced the system (from FY2009 residence tax) and set the minimum at ¥5,000; FY2011 reform lowered it to ¥2,000; FY2015 reform raised the special-deduction cap from 10% to 20% of the income levy and added the one-stop exception.

sources.title: ふるさと納税トピックス：制度改正について（2015年4月1日）
sources.publisher: 総務省 Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
sources.curationNote: April 2015 MIC topic page: the furusato nozei limit roughly doubled for donations from 2015-01-01 (FY2015 reform); one-stop exception for donations from 2015-04-01.

sources.title: 地方税法等の一部を改正する法律（令和8年3月31日法律第2号）
sources.publisher: 国立国会図書館 日本法令索引 National Diet Library
sources.curationNote: Japanese Law Index entry for 令和8年法律第2号: submitted 2026-02-20, passed and promulgated 2026-03-31. Confirms enactment; the content is described in the MIC PDF (001070694).

sources.title: 寄附金税額控除について
sources.curationNote: Takasaki City residence-tax page. FY2011 (平成23年度) reform lowered the residence-tax donation minimum from ¥5,000 to ¥2,000 from FY2012 (平成24年度) residence tax, i.e. donations made in 2011. FY2015 reform raised the special-deduction cap from 10% to 20%.

sources.title: No.1155 ふるさと納税(寄附金控除)
sources.curationNote: NTA Tax Answer: from 2015-04-01, salaried people who do not need to file a return can use the one-stop exception if they donate to 5 or fewer municipalities. Filing a return voids one-stop applications.

sources.title: 成年年齢引き下げに伴う対応について
sources.publisher: 福島銀行 The Fukushima Bank
sources.curationNote: April 2022 bank notice: NISA age requirement is 18+ as of January 1 from 2023-01-01 (20+ until 2022-12-31).

sources.title: 【重要】成年年齢の引下げに伴う当社の対応について
sources.curationNote: Feb 2022 broker notice: under the 2019 tax law revision, the lower age of adulthood applies to NISA and Junior NISA from 2023-01-01; during 2022 NISA still required age 20.

ruleVersions.statementEn: Pre-2024 NISA holdings can be kept until their original tax-exempt period ends. When the period ends they must be sold or moved to a taxable account.

ruleVersions.title: NISA for ages 0–17 (from January 2027)
ruleVersions.statementEn: From January 1, 2027, children aged 0–17 (as of January 1) can use the tsumitate quota only: up to ¥600,000 of new investment per year, with a holding limit of ¥6,000,000. From age 12, a parent or guardian can withdraw money only with the child's consent and only for the child's own purposes, such as education or living costs. At 18 the account moves automatically to the adult NISA. Enacted by 所得税法等の一部を改正する法律 (令和8年法律第12号), promulgated March 31, 2026.

ruleVersions.title: Keeping NISA when leaving Japan
ruleVersions.statementEn: Account holders who leave Japan because of an employer's transfer order (or a similar unavoidable reason, including a spouse accompanying the transferee) can keep existing NISA holdings tax-exempt by filing a continuation notice (継続適用届出書) with their financial institution by the day before departure. The exemption lasts until December 31 of the year in which five years have passed since the notice. No new purchases are allowed while abroad, and a return notice (帰国届出書) must be filed within that period, or the account is closed and the holdings move to a taxable account. People leaving for other reasons must file a departure notice, and their NISA account is closed. Not every financial institution supports the continuation procedure.

ruleVersions.title: Usable share 52.5% / cost cap 47.5% (2026-10–2027-09)
ruleVersions.statementEn: For the designation period from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, municipalities must keep at least 52.5% of donations for local use; equivalently, fundraising costs may be at most 47.5%. The required share rises each October to 60% from the 2029 designation. Legal basis: the 60% standard is in Local Tax Act (地方税法) article 37-2 as revised by 令和8年法律第2号, applied in stages by designation year (October to September); the calculation method is set by MIC notice (総務省告示). These are rules for municipalities; donors' deductions are unchanged.
